subject: ClearPath integration: escalation for duplicate webhooks and SLA coordination
thread_summary: Partner escalation: ClearPath reported duplicate webhook deliveries and 503s causing customer-impacting errors. Internal coordination to triage, deploy a canary routing change, and sign an SLA amendment with credits and rollback plan.
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearpath.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ClearPath Integrations <support@clearpath.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: [Urgent] ClearPath webhook duplicates + 503s affecting integration
Attachments: clearpath_error_log_20270427.txt (text)

Hi Irene / Sergio,

We started seeing a spike of duplicate webhook deliveries into Redwood's partner endpoint around 09:45 PT this morning. On our side the retries are firing after a short 30s backoff and we're getting 503s returned intermittently from your ingestion tier. The combination is creating duplicate create events in downstream customers and causing customer incident tickets.

Key symptoms from our logs:
- repeated 409 / duplicate-key errors followed by 503s from your endpoint
- client retries up to 3x within ~2 minutes, then a broader retry storm
- examples and stack traces attached (clearpath_error_log_20270427.txt)

We're escalating because this is hitting two joint customers and we need a coordinated mitigation that prevents duplicates without losing events. Can your team advise on an interim routing or rate-limiting configuration we should apply? We're available for a quick bridge.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Integration Lead, ClearPath Integrations
elena@clearpath.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearpath.com>, ClearPath Integrations <support@clearpath.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Urgent] ClearPath webhook duplicates + 503s affecting integration

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. We're treating this as a high-priority partner incident.

Immediate asks:
- Can ClearPath temporarily stop retries on the affected webhook (or increase retry interval to >5 minutes) while we validate our ingestion queue?
- Please share any request IDs or sample payloads for the duplicate creates (we have the logs you attached but a few request IDs would help tracing).

We're proposing the following short-term plan:
1) Redwood will enable a 10% canary routing to a variant that enforces idempotency + stricter retry smoothing (we'll manage this on our side).
2) ClearPath will deploy a patch to include an Idempotency-Key header and reduce retry aggressiveness.
3) Marissa and Vivek will coordinate a fast-track SLA amendment for partner-facing escalation credits and a defined rollback window.

Sergio — can you outline the technical steps and whether we need a config change for the canary? Marissa / Vivek — can you start the contract thread (DocuSign link ok) so procurement is looped?

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships (Integrations)
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwoodinference.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@clearpath.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Urgent] ClearPath webhook duplicates + 503s affecting integration

Thanks — quick triage notes below.

Root cause hypothesis: transient saturation in our partner ingestion pool combined with ClearPath's short retry policy. That leads to duplicate deliveries when retries occur during partial failures.

Short-term mitigations I can implement from our side (within 30–90 minutes):
- Create a canary route (10% traffic) that will: apply an idempotency window of 5 minutes, accept Idempotency-Key header, and apply a backoff-based acceptance queue.
- Temporarily lower max concurrent connections from ClearPath IPs to reduce burst saturation.
- Enable additional logging/tracing for the request IDs you provide.

We will need ClearPath to:
- Add an Idempotency-Key header to webhook payloads (uuid per event)
- Relax retry schedule to 5m / 15m / 60m for the next 72 hours

I can push the canary config now and coordinate a 2-hour monitoring window. If we see duplicates still, we will expand the canary and then roll full config.

Technical attachments: none for now — I will upload a proposed config snippet to the shared drive after the canary is live.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearpath.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ClearPath Integrations <support@clearpath.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Urgent] ClearPath webhook duplicates + 503s affecting integration

On Tue, Apr 27, 2027 at 11:10 AM Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Quick triage notes below.

Thanks for the triage and the clear mitigation steps. A couple of constraints to flag from our side:
- We can ship the Idempotency-Key change in a controlled rollout tomorrow morning (Weds 28 Apr) at 09:00 PT; our release window is constrained by downstream testing.
- We cannot fully pause retries today — the earliest we can shift retry schedule is the same Weds 09:00 PT window.
- Procurement will require an SLA amendment for partner escape credits if customers see downtime — we need the language to show explicit credit tiers and a 2-week target to finalize.

We agree to the 10% canary on your side once we push the header change. Please proceed with the canary today if it helps trace behaviour; we'll coordinate the code deploy tomorrow AM.

Elena
Elena Ruiz
Integration Lead, ClearPath Integrations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearpath.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClearPath integration: escalation for duplicate webhooks and SLA coordination

Hi Elena / team — looping procurement & account owners.

We've drafted an emergency SLA amendment that adds a partner-facing credit table scoped to webhook delivery issues. Summary of proposed terms (attached in proposed_sla_patch_v1.pdf):
- Credit tier A: 99.9% partner endpoint availability => full credit for joint-customer incidents
- Emergency rollback / canary window obligations defined (24h notice for production rollback unless mutually agreed)
- Temporary escalation credit (pro-rated) for the duration of the migration

Elena — please review the attached draft. If acceptable we can route via DocuSign (link below) and aim to have signatures by EOB tomorrow. Link: https://docusign.net/clearpath-sla-amend

I'll also coordinate a short procurement call if they need vendor-specific language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearpath.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Action plan / timeline: ClearPath webhook duplication incident

Team — summary and agreed action items after today's coordination: 

1) Immediate (today):
- Sergio to enable a 10% canary route now (monitoring window 120m).
- Sergio to add enhanced logging for request IDs and share traces to HS-987654.

2) Tomorrow morning (2027-04-28 09:00 PT):
- ClearPath to deploy Idempotency-Key header change and adjust retry schedule.
- Once ClearPath confirms deploy, Redwood will progressively increase canary to 100% over a 3-hour window if telemetry is clean.

3) Contract & credits:
- Marissa to send DocuSign for the SLA amendment (proposed_sla_patch_v1.pdf). Target: signatures by EOB 2027-04-29.

4) Rollback & escalation:
- Agreed rollback plan: Redwood will revert canary to trunk routing and notify in 30 minutes if duplicates persist.
- Both parties to maintain a 2-hour on-call window for the next 48 hours.

Can everyone please confirm the items above, and Elena please confirm availability for the 09:00 PT deploy tomorrow. Once confirmed I'll create a shared incident bridge and schedule 15-minute checkpoints.

Thanks all,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships (Integrations)
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
